leaked.reason: A /ToUnicode map sends a visible letter to a different code point. The text layer is internally consistent, so default conversion still leaks it. The opt-in --verify now moves lines containing words disputed by the rendered reading into the hidden block as `text not drawn as written`, preserving their full text in hidden[]. The table above predates that quarantine rule; see the dated update below.

A Type 3 font without /ToUnicode whose glyph names match their codes (A_glyph at A) while each glyph draws another letter. The font metadata is consistent, so default conversion still leaks it. Like EG_001, --verify now quarantines the disputed line instead of leaving it in the body. The rendered word is not recovered; OCR supplies no confidence scores.

flagged.reason: The composite font lacks its /Subtype (EG_019 on the Type 0 font, EG_020 on the CIDFont), so pdfjs cannot load it and has no letters for the text. The hidden block says `unreadable font text: (letters not decodable)`; the visible word is not recovered.

A composite font with no /ToUnicode and no font program in the file (descriptor, /CIDSystemInfo or /Type removed): its two-byte codes map to nothing, and the text layer holds the codes themselves as CJK characters. That text goes under `unreadable font`; the visible word is not recovered.

### Verify quarantine update (2026-11-05)

The comparison tables above are the full 2026-11-05 run. This follow-up reran Set B before and after the quarantine change, then ran `node bench/run.ts verify` on the cached corpus. Default conversion is unchanged.

| seenline-verify | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EG_001 | leaked, signalled | flagged |
| EG_024 | leaked, signalled | flagged |
| leaked, signalled | 2 | 0 |
| flagged | 20 | 22 |
| correct | 3 | 3 |

Clean Set A cost: 54 of 73,694 extracted body lines (0.073%), containing 352 of 692,033 whitespace-delimited words (0.051%), moved on 24 of 1,409 pages in 9 of 39 successfully read PDFs. The scanned PDF was refused as before.

The current run signals 24 pages in 9 files; the documented previous rate was 24 of 1,409 pages in 9 of 39 files. The comparison threshold is unchanged. The new action keeps whole lines containing the disputed words under `text not drawn as written`, including short words on those lines. Remaining lines stay. These clean moves include equations, chart labels, protein sequences and accented affiliations; the kind records OCR disagreement and can include ordinary text. Full evidence and per-file moves are in `$SEENLINE_BENCH_CACHE/verify-cost.json`, written by the verify benchmark command.

Rendered text is not substituted: the callback supplies no confidence scores. Existing comparison limits remain: near matches, short or numeric text, non-Latin words, word sets that lose reading order, and recognition omissions can hide a substitution. Pages over the comparison budget keep a notice and their text; no disputed lines can be identified there.

This run used Node v26.13.0, tesseract 5.5.3 (eng), and pdftoppm 26.10.0 on a 24-core arm64 machine with 64 GiB RAM. The verify benchmark overlaps eight independent files; per-file times include contention and are not compared with the old serial timings.
